task.description: Idiom/scope/decision-record hard gate (WF-02 Step 2d equivalent) on ELIXIR-DEV's ISS-0396 implementation, with an explicit independent sign-off requirement on persist/8's :event Multi-step reordering per ELIXIR-DEV's and SECURITY-REVIEWER's own flags.

result.summary:
Read the real diff (`git diff origin/main...HEAD` on task_activation.ex, sub_process.ex, engine.ex, engine_sub_process_test.exs, anti-patterns.md), the approved design (iss0396-task-records-multi-sibling-fix.md), ISS-0397's design doc, and both prior handoffs in full. Formed my own independent judgment rather than accepting either prior agent's narrative.

1) INDEPENDENT SIGN-OFF ON persist/8's :event REORDERING -- read lib/letflow/engine.ex:939-1084 myself, old and new order, line by line.
   OLD: :instance_projection (M1) -> :token_record -> children Multi.merge -> timer Multi.merge -> TaskActivation.append_multi (:task_records) -> :event -> :finalize -> audit merge.
   NEW: :instance_projection (M1) -> :event (moved here) -> :token_record -> children merge -> timer merge -> :task_records -> :finalize -> audit merge.
   Verified directly: the :event step's callback is `Multi.run(:event, fn _repo, _changes -> append_instance_started_event(instance_id, definition, correlation_key, initial_variables, pins, conflicts, attrs, prefix) end)` -- every argument is a plain local variable bound before `Multi.new()` is even called (line 953's `current_node_ids` aside, which :event does not use either). It pattern-matches `_changes` and reads zero Multi state. Moving its position in the pipe cannot change what it captures, confirmed by reading the callback body myself, not by trusting either prior summary.
   Scope of effect: this reorders every Engine.create/2 call, not only the 2+-sibling scenario. I traced every step between the old and new position for a `changes.event` reader: :token_record (reads nothing new), the two Multi.merge blocks (children merge reads `changes.token_record`/`instance_id`/`new_instance_state`/`prepared_children`/`attrs`; timer merge reads `changes.token_record`), TaskActivation.append_multi/6 (reads `changes.token_record` per its own docstring/call shape) -- none reference `changes.event`. :finalize reads only `changes.instance_projection` (its own function head: `fn repo, %{instance_projection: projection} -> ...`). The audit merge reads only `changes.finalize`. So no downstream step's behavior changes for any call shape, root or otherwise -- this is a true no-op reorder except for the one scenario it fixes.
   The fix's actual purpose, verified: EventStore.append/2's own active_instance_guard (invoked as part of the :event step) requires the instance_projections row to still be :active at INSTANCE_STARTED-append time. `SubProcess.reconcile_parent_projection/5` writes that same row's status directly (not through EventStore.append/2, so not gated by that guard) from inside the children-creation Multi.merge -- which, pre-fix, ran BEFORE :event. When 2+ synchronously-completing sibling SUB_PROCESS children exist, that write can flip the row to :completed before :event runs, and the root instance's own founding event then gets rejected as `{:instance_terminated, :completed}` -- an absurd outcome (an instance can't be born already-terminal without ever having had its founding event recorded). Moving :event to run immediately after M1, while the row is still guaranteed :active, is the correct fix, not a workaround.
   I additionally checked `finalize_instance_projection/5`'s own :active clause (engine.ex ~1344-1352): for the 2+-sibling-cascade scenario, `new_instance_state.status` (computed once, before any cascade, at initial root dispatch) is :active, so :finalize's :active clause is a no-op returning the projection struct M1 originally inserted -- unaffected by the reorder, and this no-op behavior is pre-existing, not something this diff changes. (Note, not a blocker: this means `record_instance_create_audit/3`'s `after_state` for this scenario captures the row's :active-at-M1 shape rather than the row's true final :completed status written later by SubProcess's own direct update -- but this audit-staleness question is orthogonal to the :event reordering, pre-dates ISS-0396's diff entirely since finalize's :active no-op clause and SubProcess's direct-write bypass both already existed before this branch, and is unrelated to the collision or reordering fix. Not filing as a new issue here since it needs its own root-cause trace through the ISS-0392/pre-ISS-0396 code to confirm it is not already known/accepted; flagging in this handoff's routing note for ORCH's awareness instead.)
   VERDICT: the reordering is safe, correctly targeted, and does not warrant being split into a separate follow-up issue -- it is inseparable from ISS-0396's own regression test (the test fails with `{:instance_terminated, :completed}` without it, per ELIXIR-DEV's own iteration log), so it is this issue's fix, not adjacent scope creep. I independently concur with SECURITY-REVIEWER's PASS on this point rather than deferring to it.

2) IDIOM CHECK: task_activation.ex's `key_disambiguator \\ nil` default-arg pattern matches this module's own existing style (other optional/defaulted params in the same file use the same convention). The `case key_disambiguator do nil -> ...; disambiguator -> ... end` key-computation block is idiomatic Elixir, no crutch. sub_process.ex's two join_counters fixes are one-line reuses of `SnapshotWriter.deserialize_join_counters/1` and `serialize_join_counters/1` -- the exact same public codec ISS-0397 already introduced and Engine.build_instance_state/3 already calls (verified by reading lib/letflow/design/iss0397-join-counters-fix.md:205-206,262,289) -- not a new parallel implementation. engine.ex's reorder is a pure Multi-step relocation, no new control flow. No GenServer/gen_statem/supervision code is touched anywhere in this diff -- N/A for idiom-check items 1-2 (this fix is entirely inside Engine's functional Ecto.Multi orchestration layer, not a process/state-machine module).

3) SCOPE CHECK on the 3 in-family extensions: read the new regression test (test/letflow/engine_sub_process_test.exs:1264-1330, `graph_root_split_into_two_subprocesses/1` fixture at line 316) and traced its assertions against each fix. `assert {:ok, created} = Engine.create(...)` requires the :task_records key-collision fix (core design). `assert parent_projection.status == :completed` requires both the load_parent_context/2 join_counters read fix (without it, Transition.dispatch_parallel_join/4 sees an empty join_counters map and fails the join with a misleading SUB_PROCESS_DEFINITION_NOT_FOUND error) and the reconcile_parent_projection/5 write fix (without it, sibling 2's load_parent_context/2 re-reads a stale pre-sibling-1 cohort and the join never fires, per ELIXIR-DEV's own iteration log). The `:event` reordering is required for the same assertion to not raise `{:instance_terminated, :completed}` during `Engine.create/2` itself. All 3 extensions are load-bearing for this exact test, confirmed by reading the assertions and the fix mechanisms together, not by trusting the anti-patterns.md narrative alone. None introduces a new abstraction (behaviour, macro, generic plumbing) -- all 3 are narrow, same-mechanism completions of ISS-0397's own already-approved fix shape, or a pure ordering correction. No scope creep found.

4) DECISION-RECORD CONSISTENCY: sub_process.ex's two fixes call ISS-0397's own public `SnapshotWriter.serialize_join_counters/1`/`deserialize_join_counters/1` functions verbatim (confirmed against iss0397-join-counters-fix.md's own @spec block, lines 205-206) -- no divergent codec, no re-decision of ISS-0397's design. REQ-054 (SnapshotWriter's origin requirement, docs/requirements.yaml:2869) is unaffected -- this diff only calls SnapshotWriter's already-shipped public API, adds no new function to that module. Nothing in this diff contradicts docs/migration/decisions/. No conflict found.

5) TYPE-SAFETY OBSERVATION (non-blocking, per REVIEWER's own charter item 3): `append_multi_from_existing_records/7`'s new `key_disambiguator :: term() | nil` @spec (task_activation.ex, matching the approved design's own literal spec text) is looser than necessary -- every real call site passes either `nil` or a `TokenRecord.id` (`Ecto.UUID.t()`), so `Ecto.UUID.t() | nil` would make the intended usage self-documenting and would let Dialyzer catch a future caller passing, e.g., an atom or a raw Token struct instead of a resolved TokenRecord id. This is a class of invalid input a struct/type change could make unrepresentable rather than relying on convention -- not a defect (the design itself specifies `term()`, and the current test suite exercises only the correct usage), so this does not block PASS. Per the ISSUE_QUEUE.md protocol (docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md), I did NOT self-assign a docs/issues/ISS-NNNN.yaml id myself -- that protocol was explicitly changed (2026-08-21) to require id allocation via ORCH calling letflow-queue's register_task, not a scanned/guessed number. Reporting this finding to ORCH in this handoff's routing note instead, for ORCH to register via the queue if judged worth tracking.

6) REGRESSION -- ran only the 3 specified files in the foreground, nothing broader: `mix test test/letflow/engine_sub_process_test.exs test/letflow/iss0397_join_counters_test.exs test/letflow/routers/instances_test.exs` -> `Result: 62 passed`, 0 failures. Also ran `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` (clean) and `mix format --check-formatted` (clean) myself before concluding.

Verdict: no defect found. The core fix matches the approved design exactly. All three in-family extensions are genuinely necessary (proven by tracing the regression test's own assertions against each fix's mechanism) and correctly scoped -- no premature abstraction, no framework-ahead-of-need. persist/8's reordering gets its own explicit, independently-derived sign-off above: safe, correctly targeted, appropriately kept on this branch rather than split out.
